instruction.name: vdiv.h
instruction.description: Divide each signed 16-bit element in `a` by the corresponding element in `b`.

experiments.name: operand dependency chain
experiments.init: li.d $r4, 1; vreplgr2vr.b $vr0, $r4; li.d $r4, 1; vreplgr2vr.b $vr1, $r4; li.d $r4, 1; vreplgr2vr.b $vr2, $r4

latencies.notes: Data-dependent, and a ladder rather than a set of discrete classes: latency = 5 + (64/16)*(6 + floor(bits(|quotient|)/4)), that is 5 + 4*(6 + n) with n the number of complete four-bit quotient digits. The minimum is 17 with a zero dividend and the maximum is 41 at a 15-bit quotient. LSX and LASX are identical for every element width although LASX carries twice the lanes, so the lanes and both 128-bit halves are refined in parallel and only the element width sets the per-bit rate, 16 quotient bits per cycle in aggregate. The unit divides magnitudes, skips trailing zero digits (2^40 / 1 still costs 11) and only pays for active lanes (one active lane in vdiv.bu measures 34 against 69 with every lane active). Measured with the drift-free chain `vdiv.h $xr0, $xr0, $xr1` and divisor 1, which returns the dividend unchanged. The cases array holds named sample points on this ladder, not an exhaustive classification.

throughput.command: ./bench --unroll 1000 --iters 1000 --warmup 10 --reps 7 --init 'li.w $r4, 1; vreplgr2vr.h $vr8, $r4; li.w $r4, 1; vreplgr2vr.h $vr16, $r4; li.w $r4, 1; vreplgr2vr.h $vr9, $r4; li.w $r4, 1; vreplgr2vr.h $vr17, $r4; li.w $r4, 1; vreplgr2vr.h $vr10, $r4; li.w $r4, 1; vreplgr2vr.h $vr18, $r4; li.w $r4, 1; vreplgr2vr.h $vr11, $r4; li.w $r4, 1; vreplgr2vr.h $vr19, $r4; li.w $r4, 1; vreplgr2vr.h $vr12, $r4; li.w $r4, 1; vreplgr2vr.h $vr20, $r4; li.w $r4, 1; vreplgr2vr.h $vr13, $r4; li.w $r4, 1; vreplgr2vr.h $vr21, $r4; li.w $r4, 1; vreplgr2vr.h $vr14, $r4; li.w $r4, 1; vreplgr2vr.h $vr22, $r4; li.w $r4, 1; vreplgr2vr.h $vr15, $r4; li.w $r4, 1; vreplgr2vr.h $vr23, $r4' --asm 'vdiv.h $vr0, $vr8, $vr16; vdiv.h $vr1, $vr9, $vr17; vdiv.h $vr2, $vr10, $vr18; vdiv.h $vr3, $vr11, $vr19; vdiv.h $vr4, $vr12, $vr20; vdiv.h $vr5, $vr13, $vr21; vdiv.h $vr6, $vr14, $vr22; vdiv.h $vr7, $vr15, $vr23'
throughput.notes: Range over the same pairs: min CPI 7.50 at 0/32767, max CPI 19.52 at 32767/2. Sample uses 1/1.

notes: LSX variable-latency integer divide/modulo. Latency uses an element-0 reset helper; throughput uses 8 independent lanes. Ranges cover positive operands including powers of two and max values. Both vector sources are recorded separately; they share the same result path where the hardware is symmetric.
